Re: Appeal of Medical-Necessity Denial  
Member: Reese Foster  
Member ID: W856589674  
Plan: Blue Cross Blue Shield of New Mexico Commercial/ACA  
Requested service: Shoulder labral/instability repair  
CPT: 29806  
Reference number: POC-6E764DFFE5-45256  
Date of denial notice: August 22, 2026

To the Appeals Department:

I am appealing the denial of prior authorization for CPT 29806, arthroscopic shoulder capsulorrhaphy/labral and instability repair. The denial states that the requested procedure does not meet the plan’s medical-necessity criteria.

This appeal is timely. The denial notice states that the appeal must be received by February 18, 2027.

The available clinical record supports medical necessity:

- I have experienced 14 months of recurrent shoulder-instability episodes with apprehension.
- I have had three anterior shoulder dislocations, including a most recent dislocation requiring reduction in the emergency department.
- The June 12, 2026 MR arthrogram shows an anteroinferior labral tear, specifically a Bankart lesion, with a small Hill-Sachs lesion. Glenoid bone loss is under 10 percent, and the rotator cuff is intact.
- Examination shows a positive apprehension test, positive relocation test, and increased anterior translation on load-and-shift testing. These findings document symptomatic anterior glenohumeral instability.
- The instability substantially limits function. I avoid overhead reaching and cannot return to work involving lifting.
- I completed 20 supervised physical-therapy visits over 10 weeks, from May 2 through July 11, 2026. Treatment focused on rotator-cuff and scapular-stabilizer strengthening with activity modification. The physical-therapy discharge note documents this course.
- I used NSAIDs for six months during flares. An injection was not indicated for mechanical instability caused by a Bankart lesion.
- There is no active infection or untreated substance-use issue. I am a nonsmoker, with a BMI of 29, and have full strength.

The record therefore establishes recurrent traumatic instability, objective examination findings, structural pathology on MR arthrogram, failure of supervised conservative care, and substantial impairment of work and daily activities. The requested repair is directed at the documented anteroinferior labral tear and recurrent instability rather than nonspecific shoulder pain.

I understand that BCBSNM may use a health-plan policy or delegated clinical-review criteria for this determination. I was not provided the specific policy, version, effective date, or individual criteria that the reviewer applied. The public materials I was able to locate do not establish which exact criteria governed this request. Accordingly, this appeal does not quote a BCBSNM policy. Please identify the exact medical policy or clinical-review guideline used, including its title, policy or document number, version, effective date, and the specific criterion or criteria that were considered unsatisfied.

Please also provide the clinical rationale for the denial and conduct a complete reconsideration based on the enclosed records. If the reviewer believes that the 10-week documented therapy course does not satisfy the applicable conservative-care requirement, please consider the documented three anterior dislocations, including the emergency-department reduction, the persistent instability despite therapy, and the structural Bankart lesion with Hill-Sachs lesion. Please also arrange a peer-to-peer review between the reviewing clinician and Lindqvist, MD, if available.

I request that BCBSNM overturn the denial and authorize CPT 29806. If BCBSNM continues to deny authorization, please provide a written determination explaining each unmet criterion, the evidence relied upon, the governing policy or guideline, and all further appeal or external-review rights.

Sincerely,

Reese Foster
